text: Call 911 now. Give your exact location (barangay, street, landmark), how many people are with you, and any injuries.
Stay where rescuers can find you. Signal with a flashlight, whistle, bright cloth, or by tapping on pipes or walls.
Save phone battery: lower screen brightness and send text messages if calls do not go through.
Give first aid only if you are trained: apply firm, direct pressure on bleeding wounds. Do not move a person with a suspected head, neck, or back injury unless they are in immediate danger.
Prioritize children, older adults, pregnant individuals, persons with disabilities, and anyone with medical conditions. Keep their medicines and assistive devices with them.
Do not attempt risky self-rescue through floodwater, fire, smoke, or collapsed structures.
Do not spread or act on unverified information. Rely on official advisories from the Batangas City government, CDRRMO, PAGASA, and PHIVOLCS.
Drinking water and ready-to-eat food for at least 3 days.
Maintenance medicines, prescriptions, and a first aid kit.
Flashlight, whistle, charged phone and power bank, battery-powered radio.
Important documents (IDs, certificates, insurance) in a waterproof bag, and some cash.
Extra clothing, blanket, face masks, and hygiene items.
Baby supplies, mobility aids, hearing aids, eyeglasses, and any special medical equipment.
Follow evacuation orders from the Batangas City government, CDRRMO, and your barangay officials. ALERTIFY's automated assessment does not replace official orders.
Evacuate early. People who need assistance should leave before conditions worsen — tell responders about special needs when you call.
If anyone is in immediate danger, call 911 (national emergency hotline).
Batangas City CDRRMO coordinates local rescue and evacuation — see the Emergency Contacts page.
For medical emergencies call 911 or the Philippine Red Cross (143 / Emergency Medical Services).
Water is rising — move to higher ground now if it is safe to do so. Do not wait for the water to reach your knees.

Water at waist level or higher is very dangerous. Move to the highest safe floor of a sturdy building and call for rescue instead of wading out. Avoid enclosed attics where rising water could trap you.
Turn off electricity at the main breaker and close the LPG tank only if you are standing on dry ground and it is safe to do so.
Move important documents, valuables, and emergency supplies to an upper floor or a higher place.
Monitor PAGASA rainfall/flood advisories and announcements from the CDRRMO and your barangay.
Do not walk, swim, or drive through floodwater. About 15 cm (6 in) of moving water can knock you down and 60 cm (2 ft) can sweep away a vehicle.
Stay away from electric posts, fallen wires, drainage canals, open manholes, and riverbanks.
Avoid contact with floodwater — it may be contaminated. If you waded in floodwater, especially with wounds, consult a health center about leptospirosis prevention.
Rubber boots, raincoat, and plastic bags to keep items dry.
Evacuate to a designated evacuation center when advised by authorities, or right away if you live in a low-lying or flood-prone area and the water is rising.
With water waist-deep or higher, call 911 or the CDRRMO for rescue rather than attempting to cross the water yourself.
Stay indoors in the strongest interior room, away from windows and glass doors.
Keep updated on PAGASA Tropical Cyclone Wind Signals through radio or your phone.
Your house is seriously damaged — move to the sturdiest part of the structure and request help to evacuate once it is safe to move.
Secure or move away from loose roofing and broken windows. Stay in an undamaged interior room.
Flooding is reported — follow flood safety: move to higher ground and do not cross floodwater.
Do not go outside during the storm, including during a sudden calm (the eye) — strong winds return suddenly from the opposite direction.
Stay far away from fallen trees and power lines and treat every wire as live. Report them to Meralco and the CDRRMO.
Do not use candles or open flames near curtains or light materials during power outages; use flashlights.
Battery-powered radio, extra batteries, and rain gear.
Evacuate before landfall if you live in a coastal, low-lying, or landslide-prone area or in a house made of light materials, especially when authorities order pre-emptive evacuation.
A seriously damaged house is not safe shelter. Go to an evacuation center as soon as it is safe to travel.
Report fallen or sparking power lines to Meralco (16211) and the CDRRMO.
DROP, COVER, and HOLD ON: get under a sturdy table, protect your head and neck, and hold on until the shaking stops.
Move to an open area away from buildings, trees, electric posts, and power lines. Drop down and protect your head.
Pull over in an open area away from bridges, overpasses, and posts. Stay inside with your seatbelt on until the shaking stops.
When the shaking stops, check yourself and others for injuries, then leave the building calmly using the stairs.
Expect aftershocks. Drop, cover, and hold on every time the ground shakes.
The building may be unsafe. Get out once the shaking stops and do not re-enter until it has been inspected by authorities.
If trapped under debris: cover your mouth with cloth, tap on a pipe or wall or use a whistle so rescuers can hear you. Shout only as a last resort to avoid inhaling dust.
Do not run outside while the ground is shaking.
Do not use elevators.
Do not light matches or lighters until you are sure there are no gas leaks.
Stay away from damaged buildings, walls, bridges, and steep slopes.
Sturdy shoes, hard hat or helmet if available, and dust masks.
If you are near the coast and the shaking was strong or long, move to high ground immediately — a tsunami may follow. Do not wait for an official warning.
Proceed to an open evacuation area or designated evacuation center if your building is damaged or authorities advise it.
Alert everyone around you and get out. Call 911 / BFP Batangas City once you are outside.
Stay low under the smoke and cover your nose and mouth with a damp cloth.
Before opening a door, touch it with the back of your hand. If it is hot, use another exit. Close doors behind you to slow the fire.
If you cannot get out: close the door, seal gaps with wet cloth, go to a window, signal for help, and call 911 with your exact location.
If your clothes catch fire: STOP, DROP, and ROLL.
Prepare to leave: grab your go-bag, keep exits clear, and follow instructions from the BFP.
Do not use elevators.
Do not go back inside for belongings or pets.
Do not hide in closets or bathrooms.
Never use water on electrical, LPG, or cooking-oil fires.
Do not crowd the area or block roads — fire trucks need clear access.
Go to a safe assembly area upwind and away from the fire. Do not return until the BFP declares it safe.
Call BFP Batangas City or 911 immediately, even if you think someone else has already called.
Monitor PHIVOLCS volcano bulletins for the current Alert Level and follow LGU advisories.
Stay indoors, close windows and doors, and seal gaps with damp cloth.
Wear an N95 mask (or a damp cloth if none is available) and protect your eyes with goggles. Avoid wearing contact lenses.
Heavy ash can collapse roofs. Clear ash only if it is safe, never alone, and wearing protection.
Anyone with breathing difficulty, asthma, or heart or lung conditions should stay indoors and get medical help immediately if symptoms worsen.
An evacuation order is in effect for your area — evacuate now as directed by authorities.
Do not enter restricted or permanent danger zones declared by PHIVOLCS.
Avoid driving in heavy ashfall — roads become slippery and visibility drops.
Cover water containers and food; do not use water that looks contaminated by ash.
N95 masks, goggles, and plastic covers for water and food.
Evacuate when PHIVOLCS raises the Alert Level and the LGU orders evacuation of your area.
For severe breathing difficulty call 911 or the Philippine Red Cross Emergency Medical Services.
Warning signs mean the slope may fail. Leave the area immediately and move away from the path of the slope.
Move away from the landslide area — more slides may follow. Stay clear until authorities assess it.
During continuous heavy rain, stay alert to rumbling sounds, cracking trees, tilting posts, and creek water that suddenly turns muddy or drops.
Check for injured or trapped people near the slide without entering the slide area; guide rescuers to them.
Do not cross areas with moving debris or mudflow.
Avoid river valleys and low-lying areas below slopes during heavy rain.
Stay away from damaged power lines and broken water or gas lines.
Your home is on or below a slope — evacuate pre-emptively when heavy rain warnings are issued.
Proceed to a designated evacuation center away from slopes when advised by authorities.
Move away from the immediate danger to a safe place if you can do so safely.
Call 911 and describe what is happening, where you are, and how many people are affected.
Do not approach hazardous materials, unknown substances, damaged structures, or violent situations.
Leave the area if instructed by responders or if conditions are getting worse.
